ai.description: *Chrysopelea ornata* (Colubridae) reaches 1.3 meters. It is green with black crossbars and yellow or red spots. It features a flattened belly for gliding and a distinctive black-and-yellow head pattern.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Chrysopelea ornata* is best distinguished by the distinct, large, yellow-to-green cross-bars or "flower-like" markings running down the center of its black-scaled back.
ai.habitat: *Chrysopelea ornata* inhabits moist deciduous forests, plantations, and tropical evergreen woodlands across the Indian subcontinent, typically ranging from sea level to 1,000m.
ai.behavior: *Chrysopelea ornata* is primarily diurnal, actively hunting lizards and small rodents by gliding between trees using its flattened, aerodynamic body to control descent.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Chrysopelea ornata* is oviparous, laying clutches of 6–12 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the pre-monsoon season, with hatching often observed in the summer.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Ornate Flying Snake occurs across the Western Ghats and Northeast India, typically inhabiting lowland forests and plantations from sea level up to 1,000 meters.
